title: applied-ml-weekly-notes-2026-05-26
content:
Applied ML weekly notes - 2026-05-26
Owner: Evelyn Chen (eng-applied-ml)
Collaborators: Marco Ruiz, Aisha Patel, Jonah Kim
Status: draft

Summary
- Main focus this week: quantization experiments for onboarding 34B chat models, stabilizing our eval regression suite post-optimizer changes, and a triage of a new failure mode seen in KV cache warmup with GPTQ-4bit kernels.
- Goal: produce a recommended quantization profile for 34B chat (baseline: FP16 -> target: 4-bit GPTQ where latency/cost wins without >2.5% quality delta on core evals) and get the new onboarding checklist merged.

Standup highlights (by engineer)
- Evelyn: Coordinated 34B test harness; ran baseline FP16 inference on 4xA100 across typical prompt mixes. Observed baseline latency 220ms median for 1024 seq, cost numbers captured in dashboard.
- Marco: Implemented deterministic seed handling for GPTQ quantizer (PR referenced). Reproduced earlier instability (non-deterministic logits) that correlates with kernel selection on older CUDA drivers.
- Aisha: Updated regression eval suite to include new safety and instruction-following checks (small held-out prompt set from customer comms). Added logging for per-token divergence.
- Jonah: Investigating KV cache warmup edge-case where GPTQ 4-bit model returns stale attention caches after a burst of short requests; reproduced locally and wrote minimal repro.

Experiments and results
1) GPTQ 4-bit quantization (llama-family derived 34B chat variant)
- Setup: Post-training GPTQ quantization using our gptq pipeline, with outlier-clipping 3.5 sigma, per-channel scaling, and cross-layer reorder enabled.
- Runs: 3 seeds, batch sizes 1/4/8, sequence lengths 128/512/1024.
- Metrics tracked: generation quality (instruction-following score), log-prob KL to FP16 baseline, MMLU microaverage (subset), latency p50/p95, memory footprint, and downstream safety flags.
- Key result: 4-bit GPTQ with fine-tuned reorder and per-channel scaling shows ~1.2% drop on instruction-following accuracy vs FP16 and MMLU delta within margin for 2 of 3 seeds. Latency improvement ~2.8x and GPU memory down ~60%.
- Failure mode: One seed produced larger hallucination rates for long-context (>1k tokens) conversations — correlates with kernel choice on CUDA 12.4 vs 12.3. Action: pin kernel selection in runtime or add fallback to slower but stable kernel.

2) Quantization-aware tuning (light QAT) on candidate prompts
- Quick QAT (1-2 epochs) on instruction-following synthetic dataset improved the worst-case seed to within 0.6% of FP16 on our instruction metric. Cost: small training overhead but good ROI for high-value customers.

3) Eval regression suite updates
- Added per-prompt token divergence traces and a ) delta alert threshold at 1.5% global and 3.0% per-prompt.
- CI now records token-level diffs and stores a small trace for failing prompts (max 10 prompts). Useful to triage GPTQ seed variance.

Onboarding checklist progress (model-onboarding: LL-34B-chat-candidate)
- Steps completed:
  - License and weights verified (legal ok).
  - Baseline FP16 perf runs: captured.
  - Initial GPTQ quantization: prototype run done.
  - Eval coverage: instruction, safety, MMLU subset, latency/cost metrics.
- Remaining:
  - Finalize recommended quantization profile (4-bit GPTQ + QAT fallback) and document recommended kernels by CUDA version.
  - Integrate kernel pinning/fallback into compilation layer.
  - Add model to model-catalog with verified performance profile and rollout policy.

Issues and blockers
- KV cache warmup bug: GPTQ 4-bit model returns stale attention cache after rapid short-request bursts. Repro steps attached in Jonah's minimal repro. Initial hypothesis: cache invalidation race triggered by concurrent cache reuse path in our batched runtime.
  - Next steps: add stronger cache locking in warmup path, run experiments at 10k req/s synthetic burst; plan to revert to FP16 or 8-bit for customers experiencing this in Dedicated until fix is validated.
- Non-deterministic logits across seeds due to kernel selection and CUDA driver mismatch.
  - Short-term mitigation: Surface CUDA driver+kernel version in onboarding docs and in console model profile. Add test that runs quantized model across two driver versions in CI.

Action items (owners)
- Marco: finish deterministic quantizer PR and add driver-version test to CI (due 2026-06-01). Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Jonah: finish KV cache repro and implement lock-based patch to warmup codepath; run full burst test (due 2026-05-29). Jira: JIRA-ML-1183
- Aisha: finalize updated regression suite thresholds and add per-prompt trace retention policy to Confluence onboarding checklist (due 2026-05-28).
- Evelyn: Draft model-catalog entry and recommended rollout policy + cost/latency profile, share with product for review (due 2026-06-02).

Meeting notes (weekly sync 2026-05-26)
- Discussed tradeoffs for shipping 4-bit as default for Hosted customers vs. opt-in. Product prefers opt-in with a recommended profile; Dedicated customers can opt for default 4-bit after SLA validation.
- Agreed to add a canary rollout step in Redwood Console (model route-level toggle and automatic fallback to FP16 on per-route errors). Product to spec console UX for A/B toggle.
- Security & compliance: Legal flagged a minor attribution clause for model weights; onboarding checklist updated to require license scan artifact attached.

Quick notes / TODOs
- Add a short README for quantization profiles in /models/ll-34b-chat/quantization_profile.md.
- Run full-sweep safety eval on QAT improved model next week (larger safety set).
- Coordinate with release-engineering for CUDA 12.4 kernel validation window.

References / links
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Jira: JIRA-ML-1183
- Onboarding checklist (draft): confluence.redwood/ai/onboarding-checklist

End of notes
